title: Edward Clem's street style and funeral playing
summary: Miller says he heard but never played with Clem and Manuel Perez; he discusses how Clem played in brass bands, parades and funerals.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, let's turn it back down. Okay? Go ahead, fine. Play something. Okay. One thing I wanted to ask you about was the different styles of musicians like say the ones that played funerals. Who were some of the favorite trumpet players say in the street? The olden time men back in the times of Manuel Perez and Clem. Edward Clem. Do you remember those fellas?
I remember Edward Clem and Manuel Perez. But I mean, I didn't ever play with them, you know. But I heard them playing. I think Manny Perez and Edward Clem both were real good musicians.
Well, could you give us an impression of the style that say Edward Clem played on your horn?
Well, all I know he had about years time.
stuff a popular tune from that era. Yeah, that's where it came out. Well, who did he play with? Did he play with dance bands or brass bands or both or what?

Well, he played with brass bands. I know he played with brass bands. I don't know if he worked at the Lyrica Robichaux or not some time back. Did he play pretty much the same in the street? No, like he did at dance? Well, no, it would be a little different. It would be a little different. You know, parades and dance music would be a little different, you know. What kind of numbers would he be featured on in parades? Well, tell the truth, I wouldn't know, but all I know in the streets how you played, I never did. You haven't played a dance. No, I never did. But I pretty much got an idea that he played that type of music back then, you know. They played KKKKD in the streets. Yeah, they played that on parades. That was like a march, right?

And did you ever hear him play any funeral numbers? Yeah. Was he featured as a trumpet solo? Yeah, he was playing the first trumpet, I think. Yeah. Do you remember his style on a, say, some slow tempo thing? Yeah, I was playing the dirt.
